correctness.rationale: The two-point difference is exactly (u·x)u on the quadratic. For eta=1/d its update is the orthogonal projector I-uu^T/d. Second-moment contraction is 1-1/d. For odd d, integral numerator products reduce modulo 2 to the nonzero idempotent (I+J)e_i. Hadamard rows give a zero projector product; repeated independent blocks imply almost-sure finite stopping with the given tail. Rank-drop equality in d steps forces orthogonality of all d sign directions. verify.py passed 659 exact rational/integer package checks before acceptance.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies a qualitative, exact arithmetic algorithmic distinction invisible to the identical mean-square rate across dimensions: odd dimensions cannot terminate from coordinate starts at all, while Hadamard dimensions terminate in finite random time almost surely. It supplies a stopping-time benchmark and structural criterion for finite-support randomized directional solvers, not an isolated constant or routine numerical gain.
